description: One PR a month carrying every update, majors included, and no automerge: a person reads each bump.
A release ages 7 days before it is proposed, so a freshly published (possibly compromised) version is not pulled in at once.

customManagers.description: mise itself, which bin/install_check_tools.sh downloads before mise.toml can be read.
The Homebrew installer, which has no releases: pinned to a commit on its default branch, aged by the commit date.

zsh plugins, pinned to a commit on the branch the trailing comment names. github-digest, not git-refs: it dates each commit, so minimumReleaseAge applies (measured from the commit date, not from when it reached the branch).
tmux plugins, same pinning as the zsh plugins above.
The Neovim release CI tests against, which it downloads rather than installs from a package manager.

pip-compile.description: The translator's Python deps. Renovate bumps the pins in hammerspoon/requirements.in (7-day age) and regenerates this lock, hashes included; indirect deps resolve to whatever PyPI has at that moment.

pip_requirements.description: Off: its only match is the lock above, which pip-compile owns; a second manager would bump versions without regenerating the hashes.

packageRules.description: Python gets its own PR: a new minor often ships before pyyaml has wheels for it, which breaks the pipx: tools' mise lock, and in the shared PR that red hides every other bump.
GitHub-hosted runner labels have no release date, so the 7-day age would hold them back forever; the datasource lists a release only once GitHub drops its beta tag.
Biome tags each release as @biomejs/biome@X.Y.Z, alongside tags for its other packages.
